subject: Proposal: Q3 spike temporary top-up and co-term
messages:
From: Jared Kim <jared.kim@brightlyhealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lowe <sarah.lowe@brightlyhealth.com>
Date: 2025-08-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Need temporary capacity for Q3 spike + co-term alignment

Hey Tessa,

Quick note — we expect a short but material increase in inference volume in early September tied to a marketing pilot (roughly 3–4x baseline for ~6 weeks). Our current contract runs through 2026-01-01. Before we start the pilot, we want to understand:

- Can Redwood provide a timeboxed top-up (temporary committed capacity or burst) for the pilot window?
- If we prefer a committed uplift, can that be co-termed to our existing renewal (2026-01-01) rather than creating a separate 12-month commitment?
- Any path to get a middle-ground price (we're not asking for full committed discount but something better than on-demand burst rates).

We’re evaluating two internal options: purely burst (pay-as-you-go), or a 6-month bridge commitment that we then fold into our renewal. If there’s a short-term amendment template and ballpark pricing, that’d be great — legal will need a quick turnaround.

Cc’ing Sarah who is managing procurement on our side.

Thanks,
Jared
Jared Kim
Sr. Product Manager, Brightly Health
jared.kim@brightlyhealth.com


From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Kim <jared.kim@brightlyhealth.com>
Cc: Sarah Lowe <sarah.lowe@brightlyhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-08-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Need temporary capacity for Q3 spike + co-term alignment

Hi Jared — thanks for the heads up. Short answer: yes, we can support both patterns. Below are two clean options and a suggested next step. I’ve attached a one-page amendment (Brightly_Amendment_v1.pdf) that sketches the bridge terms.

Option A — Short burst (no long-term uplift)
- Short-term burst pool for pilot window (6 weeks)
- Pricing: on-demand rate + 25% premium for guaranteed burst capacity
- No contract amendment required; invoiced post-pilot
- Quickest to spin up (24–48 hours)

Option B — 6-month bridge commitment (recommended if you want predictable unit pricing)
- Commit to an uplifted committed capacity for 6 months (Aug 20 — Feb 20)
- Discount: 12% off hosted per-token list for committed uplift portion
- Bridge will be co-termed/annualized into your existing renewal so final contract still ends 2026-01-01 (we'll pro-rate the bridge portion in the first renewal invoice)
- Includes 30% priority burst headroom during pilot (maintains latency SLO)

Tradeoffs
- Option A: fastest, but more expensive on a per-token basis.
- Option B: slightly more paperwork, better unit economics, predictable spend; co-term handled via amendment and pro-rated credit at renewal.

Next steps
1) If you pick Option B, we’ll prepare a short amendment and routing to Legal + DocuSign (I attached a draft).
2) I can schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk numbers and timing with your procurement.

Questions (to help pricing if you prefer Option B)
- Estimated extra daily tokens during pilot (avg and peak)?
- Any PO/invoice timing constraints?

Thanks — happy to hop on a call.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: 415-555-0192
E: tessa.morgan@redwood.ai

Attachments: Brightly_Amendment_v1.pdf (draft amendment, pricing table)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Jared Kim <jared.kim@brightlyhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-08-18T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Need temporary capacity for Q3 spike + co-term alignment

Looping in a quick commercial note — Jared, appreciate the context. Building on Tessa’s Option B, here’s a pragmatic structure we’ve used for similar pilots:

Pilot Bridge (preferred)
- Term: 6 months (start date aligned to pilot kick-off)
- Committed uplift volume: agreed uplift bucket (we’ll use your expected avg x1.5 as a baseline)
- Discount structure: 10–15% off hosted list for bridge capacity depending on uplift size — for Brightly I recommend 12% (we can move to 14% at uplift > 2.5x baseline)
- Billing: pro-rated on signature, invoiced monthly; any unused committed tokens during bridge can be carried forward into renewal as a credit or converted into a blended top-up at renewal (we'll put the mechanism in the amendment)

Operational notes
- We need procurement to confirm PO timing for invoice cadence — Karthik, can you confirm whether Brightly prefers monthly invoices or net-30 consolidated?
- Legal: the amendment in Tessa’s attachment is intentionally short (one page). Legal redlines are usually limited to indemnity language and data-retention clauses.

If that looks acceptable I’ll draft the pricing table and we’ll update the amendment for signature.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Sales — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Thanks everyone — we reviewed options with procurement and legal. We’ll proceed with the Pilot Bridge (Option B) at the 12% uplift discount you recommended. A few final asks before signature:

- Please send the finalized amendment via DocuSign (we need a legally executed amendment to start).
- Billing: Brightly prefers monthly invoices on net-30. Please set invoice cadence to monthly pro-rated starting on the amendment signature date.
- Compliance: our security team asked for confirmation that audit logs for inference requests (retention 90 days) will be available for SOC review; can you confirm? If you can share the one-page amendment + an updated usage snapshot, we’ll route to Legal and sign.

I’ve attached our May usage for reference (usage_report_May2025.csv).

Appreciate the quick turn — looking forward to getting this live.

Best,
Jared
Sr. Product Manager, Brightly Health
